# yamt

<img src="src-tauri/icons/icon.svg" width="150" />

_A three-way merge window like the one in JetBrains IDEs, for every git conflict at once. 🔀_

</div>

&nbsp;

## Why does this exist?
1. JetBrains IDE's three-pane merge window is the only merge tool I find usable. VS Code's merge editor, its extensions and the TUI mergetools all felt unintuitive.
2. They all start from the `<<<<<<<` conflict markers. Once git has collapsed a merge into markers the base is gone, so you can see _that_ two sides differ but not _what each side changed_. yamt never parses a conflict marker: it reads the base, your side and theirs from git's index and diffs them itself.
3. `git mergetool` opens one file at a time, and real merges touch many files. yamt takes over the whole merge: every conflicted file in one window, your side on the left, theirs on the right, the result in the middle.

## Install

Download from the [releases page](../../releases):

- **Linux**: the `.AppImage` or the `.deb`. The `.deb` (`sudo apt install ./yamt_0.4.2_amd64.deb`)
  puts `yamt` on your PATH. For the AppImage, put it there yourself.

  Without AppImageLauncher:

  ```sh
  install -Dm755 yamt_0.4.2_amd64.AppImage ~/.local/bin/yamt
  ```

  With AppImageLauncher (it stops a copy outside its folder with a dialog): let it integrate the
  AppImage (it moves the file to `~/Applications` and adds a hash to the name) and link the moved
  file:

  ```sh
  ail-cli integrate yamt_0.4.2_amd64.AppImage
  mkdir -p ~/.local/bin && ln -sf ~/Applications/yamt_0.4.2_amd64_*.AppImage ~/.local/bin/yamt
  ```

  If `yamt` is then not found, `~/.local/bin` is not on your PATH: add
  `export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"` to your shell's start-up file (`~/.bashrc`, `~/.zshrc`).

- **Arch Linux**: the AppImage, or build from source (below).
- **macOS**: the `.dmg`; drag yamt to Applications. The build is not signed, so macOS refuses to open it
  ("damaged", or "could not verify … free of malware") until you clear the download mark from the whole app.
  Do this after every install or update:

  ```sh
  xattr -cr /Applications/yamt.app
  ```

  Then put `yamt` on your PATH (once):

  ```sh
  sudo mkdir -p /usr/local/bin && sudo ln -sf /Applications/yamt.app/Contents/MacOS/yamt /usr/local/bin/yamt
  ```

- **Windows 10/11**: the `_x64-setup.exe`; it installs for your user only, without admin rights.
  The build is not signed, so SmartScreen may warn: More info → Run anyway. yamt needs
  [Git for Windows](https://git-scm.com/download/win) (`git.exe` on your PATH). The installer does
  not put `yamt` on your PATH: add the folder its setup page installed to (under Windows'
  Environment Variables, user `Path`), then open a new terminal. yamt is a console program: run it
  from a terminal in the repository; started from the Start menu a console window opens beside it.

## Use

When `git merge`, `git rebase`, `git cherry-pick`, `git revert` or `git am` stops with conflicts, run `yamt` in the repository (or `yamt --repo <path>` from anywhere). It starts from a terminal; double-clicking it shows nothing.

1. Click a file in the list on the left. Your own work is on the left, what comes in on the right, the result in the middle.
2. Each change has an arrow that applies it to the result and a × that ignores it. The result is a normal editor too.
3. **Mark resolved** saves and stages the file, then opens the next one.
4. When every file is resolved, **Continue** (**Commit merge** for a merge) runs git's own continue and shows the next conflicts, if any. yamt closes when git is done.

| Key | Does |
| --- | --- |
| Enter / Backspace | apply / ignore the change (click a side first) |
| Up / Down | previous / next change |
| Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Shift+Z | undo / redo |
| Ctrl+S | save without staging, to come back later |
| Ctrl+B | hide or show the file list |
| hold Alt | minimap of the result |

Cmd for Ctrl and Option for Alt on macOS; settings (the gear) can change every key. Dragging over several changes, collapsed lines, Abort, remembered `rerere` resolutions and the rest: [the guide](docs/guide.md).

## Language servers

yamt runs the language servers your project already has, so the result pane shows their problems as you type: an underline, with the message on hover. It finds these in the repository's projects and asks once per repository whether to start them; settings can change the answer and switch off any server it found, each on its own, for that repository:

- JavaScript and TypeScript: oxlint, oxfmt, Biome, TypeScript, eslint; `.vue` files through TypeScript when the project has `@vue/typescript-plugin`
- Rust: rust-analyzer · Go: gopls · C and C++: clangd, with a compile database
- Python: ruff, ty, basedpyright, pyright
- PHP: Phpactor, with the project's own PHPStan, Psalm, PHP-CS-Fixer and phpcs; else Intelephense

Left of the gear, one **Servers** button holds every server: its drop-down lists each with its state; choose one to start, stop or restart it or to read its log. The pin next to a server puts that server's own button in the header (none at first, remembered per repository). A server the project uses but that is not installed shows "Not installed" with the install command for that language's installer (your package manager, uv, Poetry or PDM, rustup, `go install`); yamt starts it when you come back to the window. With a formatter running (oxfmt, Biome, rustfmt, gofmt, ruff, clang-format with a `.clang-format`, PHP-CS-Fixer or phpcbf, or an added server that formats), Ctrl+S formats the result before saving and leaves changes that still wait as they are. yamt ships no language server.

Other servers are added in settings under **Language servers → Added by you**: pick one **From the list** (Deno and bash-language-server are there too) or type a command and the file types it serves. yamt looks for a program in the project's `node_modules/.bin`, `.venv/bin` and `vendor/bin` up to the repository root, then on the PATH of the terminal it was started from, then in `~/go/bin`, `~/.cargo/bin`, `~/.local/bin` and Composer's global folder; a command with a `/` is read from the repository root. An added server is offered in every repository and runs where the repository's answer is Start; press **Start** under "This repository" if it is not.

## Make it feel built in

```sh
git config --global alias.resolve '!yamt'
git resolve
```

`git mergetool` is not the way to start yamt: it runs the tool once per file, while yamt handles all files in one window.

## Build from source

You need the Rust toolchain from `rust-toolchain.toml` (installed by [rustup](https://rustup.rs) on the first `cargo` call), [pnpm](https://pnpm.io), and on Linux webkit2gtk-4.1 (Arch: `webkit2gtk-4.1`; Debian/Ubuntu: `libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev`).

```sh
cargo install tauri-cli --version 2.12.1
pnpm -C frontend install
cargo tauri build
```

The bundles land in `target/release/bundle/`.

## NVIDIA on Linux

WebKitGTK's DMABUF renderer crashes on some NVIDIA setups. yamt switches it off by itself when the NVIDIA driver is loaded; a value you set for `WEBKIT_DISABLE_DMABUF_RENDERER` wins.
